question: The mean of a data is 42 and its median is 53. The mode (using empirical relation) of the data is :-
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**. Substitute the given values: **Mode = 3(53) − 2(42)**. **Mode = 159 − 84 = 75**. **∴ The correct answer is 75.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mean** of the data = 42 **Median** of the data = 53 **Formula Used:** The **empirical relationship** between the measures of central tendency is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a0d4b4af2b93b80c22e4849615bf10c9633e9661c10011e7f543269b2ae317e.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ Mode = 3 × 53 − 2 × 42 ⇒ Mode = 159 − 84 ⇒ Mode = 75 **∴ The correct answer is 75.** **__Additional Information__** Symmetrical Distribution In a **perfectly symmetrical distribution**, the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode). Skewed Distribution For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the **empirical formula** provides an approximate relationship: Mode ≈ 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.
